The card returns every edge in a repeated pair, first ones included: 1 to 5." width="100%"} Returns a list of edge IDs that represent multiple/duplicate edges. These edges share the same source and target nodes as another edge in the graph. This is useful for detecting and cleaning multigraphs. For undirected graphs, edges `(u,v)` and `(v,u)` are considered the same pair. When multiple edges exist between a pair, all edge IDs (including the first) are returned. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [list[int]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : List of edge IDs representing multiple edges. Empty if no duplicates exist. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} Groups edges by their endpoint pair and returns the flat list of edge IDs for any pair sharing more than one edge, including the earliest (canonical) representative. Directedness matters: on directed graphs $(u, v)$ and $(v, u)$ are treated as distinct pairs, so antiparallel edges do not count as duplicates; the undirected case treats them as the same. Self-loops are ignored here even when duplicated, since `which_loops()` handles those separately, so this is the right diagnostic to run before calling `remove_duplicate_edges()` or `simplify()`. ## Examples {.doc-examples} Adding the same edge more than once creates duplicates; every occurrence of a duplicated pair is returned, including the first: ::: {#ff9b1a6a .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec g = ec.Graph(directed=True) g.add_nodes(["Alice", "Bob", "Carol"]) g.add_edges( [ ("Alice", "Bob", 1.0), ("Alice", "Bob", 2.0), # Duplicate connection ("Alice", "Bob", 3.0), # Another duplicate ("Bob", "Carol", 1.0), # Single edge ] ) # Returns 3 (all Alice -> Bob edges) len(g.which_multiple()) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` 3 ``` ::: ::: A simple graph with no repeated connections has no multiple edges, which makes this a quick way to validate graph simplicity: ::: {#15a7f045 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} g = ( ec.Graph(directed=False) .add_nodes(["A", "B", "C"]) .add_edges([("A", "B"), ("B", "C"), ("C", "A")]) ) # Returns True: no duplicate edges len(g.which_multiple()) == 0 ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` True ``` ::: :::
